meta.titre: Structuring an opinion essay in English

sections.contenu_markdown: An opinion essay is not a list of random thoughts: it is a position, defended by clear reasons, each backed by a concrete example.

items: Basic paragraph structure (topic sentence + supporting details)
Linking words (first, secondly, however, in conclusion)

sections.contenu_markdown: An opinion essay should include: an introduction stating the writer's position clearly, a body with two or three distinct reasons, each illustrated with a concrete example, an acknowledgement of the opposite view if relevant, and a conclusion restating the opinion without repeating the introduction word for word.

sections.enonce_markdown: Structure an essay on 'modern or traditional medicine, which do you prefer?'

etapes.action: State the position in the introduction

etapes.resultat_markdown: In conclusion, I prefer modern medicine

sections.conclusion_markdown: The essay follows a clear position → reasons → conclusion structure.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving reasons without any concrete example to illustrate them.
items.pourquoi_faux: A reason without an example remains abstract and less convincing; examples make the argument concrete and memorable.
items.correction_markdown: Always follow each reason with at least one specific, concrete example.

items.enonce_markdown: Write one reason (with an example) to support the opinion that reading is beneficial.
items.solution_markdown: Reading improves vocabulary; for example, students who read regularly often perform better in written exams.

items_markdown: Two or three reasons, each with a concrete example
Conclusion that restates the position without repeating word for word
